profiles.name: Kareem Dewayne Jefferson
profiles.description: On August 24, 2020 Kareem Dewayne Jefferson, 20, of Los Angeles, CA pled "no contest" to a charge of looting and was sentenced to 6 months county jail. He was arrested in Los Angeles by the "Safe LA Task Force" after the George Floyd Protests.
profiles.finding: Exact and shortened LA looting queries yielded no verified portrait; Houston Kareem Jefferson age37 in2013 rejected.

profiles.name: Kelsey Donnel Jackson
profiles.description: Kelsey Jackson, 28, of Charleston, SC pled guilty to arson of a Charleston Police Department patrol car on May 30, 2020. Sentenced to 24 months federal prison plus $1,224.06 restitution (joint and several with Guthrie and Jenkins) and 3 years supervised release.
profiles.finding: Live5 sentencing article corroborates case but no identified portrait in article body.

profiles.name: Keyondre Robinson
profiles.description: Keyondre Robinson, an 18-year-old from Buffalo, New York, was among those federally prosecuted after the May 30, 2020 George Floyd protests in Buffalo. Outside the Robert H. Jackson United States Courthouse, he threw a water bottle that struck a Deputy United States Marshal in the face. Charged with assaulting a federal officer, he pleaded guilty on December 22, 2020; the charge carried a maximum of one year in prison, and he was reported to have been sentenced to a year of supervised release.
profiles.finding: Buffalo case-list corroboration; unrelated Keyondre Young/Robinson combinations rejected.

profiles.name: Killian F. Melecio
profiles.description: On May 31, 2020 following protests in Trenton, NJ, Killian Melecio, Kadeem Dockery, and Justin Spry were seen on video attempting to set fire to a police car. Dockery threw an explosive device through the open driver's window; Melecio attempted to put a shirt in the gas tank and light it on fire. Sentenced to 28 months federal prison plus 3 years supervised release.
profiles.finding: DOJ complaint identifies surveillance evidence, no suitable verified portrait yet.

profiles.name: Lamar Taylor
profiles.description: Lamar Taylor, 23, was charged with arson after allegedly setting fire to a Chicago Transit Authority van during a 2020 protest in response to the death of George Floyd. Sentenced to 26 months federal prison.
profiles.finding: Chicago CTA query unresolved; older Notre Dame and Florida namesakes rejected.

profiles.name: Lashawn L. Wilks
profiles.description: Lashawn L. Wilks, 31, of Centralia, IL was charged by federal complaint with unlawful possession of a firearm by a prohibited person after multiple sources reported he had guns at a May 23, 2020 house party and threatened to "kill a cop." After George Floyd's death he allegedly posted on Facebook threatening violence to police. On June 2, 2020 law enforcement learned he was discussing plans to organize a protest and cause a riot in Centralia, with a list of officers to shoot. A federal search of his residence found a 9mm pistol, a rifle, and a 12-gauge shotgun. Charges later dropped.
profiles.finding: DOJ Centralia case and appeal found, no portrait verified.

profiles.name: Marc Bell Gonzales
profiles.description: On May 28, 2020 as part of ongoing protests sparked by George Floyd's murder, Marc Bell Gonzales engaged with other individuals in conduct designed to accelerate a fire in the Wells Fargo Bank building in south Minneapolis. Sentenced to 37 months federal prison plus 3 years supervised release.
profiles.finding: FOX9 case article lead remains; no portrait verified this pass.

profiles.name: Michael Rodriguez
profiles.description: In 2020 in Brooklyn, NY, Michael Rodriguez, 32, a homeless man, was charged with attempting to damage government property by fire — accused of setting fire to a vehicle with an NYPD placard on a residential block. Charges later dropped; Rodriguez was misidentified as the perpetrator by police.
profiles.finding: FOX5 case dismissal report uses actual arsonist surveillance image; explicitly reject because Rodriguez was misidentified.

profiles.name: Michele Alfaro
profiles.description: On May 13, 2021 Michele Alfaro, 24, pled "no contest" to a charge of looting and was sentenced to 1 year county jail. Alfaro was arrested in Los Angeles by the "Safe LA Task Force" after the George Floyd Protests.
profiles.finding: Exact and LA query yielded unlinked professional-directory namesakes; no portrait.

profiles.name: Reza Sarhangpour Kafrani
profiles.description: Reza Sarhangpour Kafrani, also known as Reza Sarhang, is an Iranian citizen who was living in Montreal when a federal grand jury in Washington indicted him on July 30, 2021. The indictment alleged a conspiracy to export laboratory equipment from the United States to Iran through Canada and the United Arab Emirates, export-control violations, failure to file export information and money laundering. Public records do not establish that he was arrested, extradited or confined in the United States. President Joe Biden granted him a full pardon on September 14, 2023, before trial.
profiles.finding: Journal de Montreal explicitly captions subject, credits Reza Sarhang/Facebook; original1882x1338 portrait verified. Later2024 reporting suggests custody biography warrants review; no unrelated field changed.

profiles.name: Ricardo Densmore
profiles.description: Ricardo Densmore, 24, of Las Vegas was charged with co-defendants Tyree Walker and Devarian Haynes for conspiracy to commit arson and arson after he filmed Walker and Haynes setting a police car on fire on May 30, 2020. Sentenced to 24 months federal prison.
profiles.finding: Type Investigations and Las Vegas Sun corroborate case; no identified portrait accepted.

profiles.name: Rowan M. Olsen
profiles.description: Rowan M. Olsen, 19, interfered with FPS and U.S. Marshals at protests around the Hatfield Federal Courthouse in Portland, OR. Olsen entered the building and used his body to push on and hold a door closed, preventing officers from exiting; the glass door broke, injuring a deputy U.S. Marshal. He gave authorities a fake name ("Kiefer Alan Moore") and fake age and was already on probation for an earlier officer-attack conviction. Charged but not tried.
profiles.finding: Portland sources corroborate case; tennis recruit and alumni directory not sufficiently linked.

profiles.name: Scott Scelye
profiles.description: Scott Scelye appears on incarcerated-person contact lists associated with political prisoner support efforts and is listed as being held at USP Marion. Beyond these listings, there is limited publicly available information detailing the circumstances of his arrest, charges, or activism.
profiles.finding: Exact name and prisoner query found no verified portrait; spelling/identity unresolved.

profiles.name: Shant Singh Ahuja
profiles.description: On July 4, 2020 Shant Singh Ahuja, 28, of Oceanside, CA was accused of willfully destroying a closed-circuit video camera mounted on the exterior of the Hatfield Federal Courthouse in Portland, OR. Charged but not tried.
profiles.finding: Indian Panorama corroborates Portland camera charge; no portrait verified.

profiles.name: Shawn Collins
profiles.description: Shawn Collins was arrested in Philadelphia on June 2, 2020, during the citywide curfew that followed the George Floyd protests. Police responding to a report about an ATM found a loaded handgun in his waistband. Because of a prior felony conviction, he was charged federally with possessing a firearm as a felon. Collins later pleaded guilty and was sentenced to 18 months in prison. Public reporting and contemporaneous prisoner-support records establish that he remained in federal custody while the case was pending, but the exact release date has not yet been established.
profiles.finding: Philadelphia appellate opinion corroborates case; Kentucky/Florida/Ohio and football namesakes excluded.

profiles.name: Simon Habonimana
profiles.description: Simon Habonimana, 22, was charged in Fargo, ND with arming rioters, attempting to commit assault, rioting, and disobedience of public safety orders after he was arrested in connection with a protest related to the murder of George Floyd on May 30, 2020. Sentenced to 3.4 months in North Dakota state prison.
profiles.finding: VNL article connects Fargo defendant to MSUM football. Downloaded image is low-native-resolution two-view booking composite; rejected for portrait use. MSUM2019 roster confirms named player but image:null. DOB2004 on profile conflicts with age22in2020; flag separate data review.

profiles.name: Steven Lopez
profiles.description: Shot and killed photographer Tyler Gerth at a June 2020 Louisville protest; first-degree manslaughter + 22 counts wanton endangerment. Sentence: 30 years prison. Verified via public court/press records: https://www.lpm.org/news/2024-02-14/man-sentenced-to-30-years-in-prison-for-killing-louisville-photographer-tyler-gerth
profiles.finding: WAVE3 named defendant image lead identified; separate victim/athlete/Central Park and other namesakes rejected; portrait retrieval pending.

profiles.name: Taimane Jame Teo
profiles.description: On July 5-6, 2020 Taimane Jame Teo, 24, of Eugene, OR was accused of assaulting federal officers with high-intensity lasers during ongoing Portland protests after George Floyd's murder. Charged but not tried.
profiles.finding: Court exhibit calls subject Zouk and mentions2020 fundraiser; direct portrait source unresolved.

profiles.name: Tandre Buchanan
profiles.description: Tandre Buchanan Jr., 22, of Cleveland, OH was charged with interference with commerce by robbery after being identified through surveillance footage as participating in damaging businesses. He was seen breaking a glass window with a stool. The indictment alleges that on May 30, 2020 he aided and abetted others in unlawfully obstructing commerce by means of robbery against Colossal Cupcakes employees in downtown Cleveland against the will of the employees by means of actual and threatened force. Sentenced to 48 months federal prison plus 3 years supervised release.
profiles.finding: News5 Cleveland identifies orange-sweatshirt subject in FBI image; image quality/source verification pending.

profiles.name: Terrance Lee Hester
profiles.description: Terrance Lee Hester Jr., 20, of Tampa, FL was charged with arson after a May 30-31, 2020 protest near a shopping plaza on East Fowler Avenue devolved into civil unrest, looting, and destruction. Video showed Hester tossing a flaming piece of cloth through a broken window of the Champs Sports store; the building was fully engulfed and the plaza suffered ~$1.25 million in damage. Sentenced to 60 months federal prison plus 36 months supervised release.
profiles.finding: DOJ complaint and Epoch Times caption identify mugshot plus action composite; original single portrait source pending.
